The X-Y Position Indicator for a Display System was the original name given to the device invented by Douglas Engelbart in the 1960s. This device is now universally known as the computer mouse.

All three agents have provided the same answer with high confidence, and this aligns with the historical record. The patent filed by Engelbart used this formal technical name, but the device became commonly known as a "mouse" due to its appearance (with the cord resembling a tail).

Answer: Mouse
Confidence: 0.95
